Maple Materials Announces Major Expansion in Pakistan’s Construction Sector

Maple Materials, a leading supplier in Pakistan’s construction materials industry, has announced plans for a substantial expansion of its manufacturing facilities in the Punjab province. The initiative, unveiled at a press conference in Lahore on Wednesday, is expected to boost local production capacity, create hundreds of jobs, and further solidify the region’s role as a hub for the nation’s building sector.

The company confirmed that it will invest an estimated PKR 3.2 billion in the construction of a new state-of-the-art facility on the outskirts of Faisalabad. The plant will focus on the production of high-grade cement, concrete blocks, and pre-fabricated structural components for the fast-growing housing and infrastructure markets.

Speaking at the launch event, Maple Materials CEO Tariq Hussain stated, “This investment is a reflection of our confidence in Pakistan’s construction industry and its resilient workforce. By increasing our capacity, we aim to serve the growing demand for quality construction materials as the country embarks on major infrastructure projects.”

Industry analysts note that the move comes amid a steady uptick in domestic demand for construction inputs, driven by government-backed housing schemes and private sector development. Samina Qureshi, an independent construction sector analyst based in Lahore, commented, “The expansion by Maple Materials could set a precedent for further investments, especially as urbanization continues and infrastructure priorities remain high on the government’s agenda.”

According to the Pakistan Constructors’ Association, the construction materials sector contributes nearly 10 percent to the national GDP and employs over 7 million people. Local officials anticipate that the new facility will generate at least 400 direct jobs and support additional employment in transportation and related services.

Muhammad Alam, a representative of the Punjab Board of Investment and Trade, welcomed the announcement, saying, “This expansion aligns perfectly with our regional development goals. We are committed to facilitating such investments that foster economic growth and skills development in our communities.”

Construction of the new plant is set to begin in August, with operations expected to commence by the end of next year. Maple Materials has also pledged to adopt environmentally sustainable practices in the new facility, including the use of energy-efficient equipment and responsible sourcing of raw materials.
